items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had some arrangements that were made by a trombone player from South America named Bill Tamper whom I had met during my stay in Paris... Bill Tamper, the South American trombone man and arranger was also hired for this gig... I had Bill Tamper to arrange the numbers and also play trombone.

ctx.x: Fred Palmer was to join me in Bern because he had finished his job in Germany. I engaged a pianist from Martinique named Pierre Jean Louis who had a style of playing that was a little like Theolionus Monk, but with more technique. Pierre was a big fellow who could drink his share of juice and some of mine, but was never drunk and always in good humour. Georgie Smith was back again on drums. A bass player named Alvin "Buddy" Banks had received his discharge from the army in Germany and had come to Paris where I…

We opened at the Chikito the 1st of December and finished the 31st of March, 1951. I had a concert in Brussels, Belgium at the Palais des Beux-Arts and played concerts with my group in Geneva, Bienne, Zurich, Neuchatel and Luzern. These dates taken place between the 2nd and 16th of April. I had a contract to play at the cinema Rex in Zurich for 11 days starting the 16th of April. I was having a longer and more successful run with this orchestra then I did with the first one. I had some arrangements that were made…

We had played the Jazz club of Luzern the 12th of April and coming back to Bern which was still our jumping off point in Switzerland, I told the fellows that we would play the Rex starting the 16th. Georgie Smith said that he was not going unless he saw my contract. I thought he was kidding because he or anyone else had never said anything like that to me and I had never heard any musician ask the leader to let him see his contract. I ask him what did he mean and he said: 'Put the contract on the table,' which…
